---
title: "The Julia package registry"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Julia's [General registry](https://github.com/JuliaRegistries/General) is a
git repository of TOML files: an index of every registered package, and four
small files per package. This article reads all of them with zutoml and asks
what they say, in particular which packages carry code compiled from C, C++
or Fortran.

```{r setup}
library(zutoml)
```

## Fetch the registry

The registry is downloaded once, as a tarball of a pinned commit (about
12 MB), and unpacked into a temporary directory.

```{r}
commit <- "19314165a0b3aaf26cba8eb458327ec2f90dce4d"
url <- paste0("https://codeload.github.com/JuliaRegistries/General/tar.gz/", commit)
tarball <- tempfile(fileext = ".tar.gz")
withr::with_options(list(timeout = 300), download.file(url, tarball, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb"))
dir <- tempfile("General")
untar(tarball, exdir = dir)
root <- list.files(dir, full.names = TRUE)
```

## The index

`Registry.toml` names the registry and lists every package by UUID, each an
inline table with its name and the directory holding its files:

```{r}
toml_read(file.path(root, "Registry.toml"), select = "repo")
index <- toml_read(file.path(root, "Registry.toml"), select = "packages")
length(index)
index[1:2]
```

A data frame is easier to work with:

```{r}
pkgs <- data.frame(
  uuid = names(index),
  name = vapply(index, `[[`, "", "name"),
  path = vapply(index, `[[`, "", "path"),
  row.names = NULL
)
pkgs$jll <- endsWith(pkgs$name, "_jll")
table(pkgs$jll)
```

Packages whose names end in `_jll` are binary wrappers. Each is built by
[BinaryBuilder](https://docs.binarybuilder.org) from a recipe in
[Yggdrasil](https://github.com/JuliaPackaging/Yggdrasil) and ships a compiled
library or program, usually written in C, C++ or Fortran.

## One package: Xsum

[Xsum.jl](https://github.com/JuliaMath/Xsum.jl) gives exactly rounded sums
through Radford Neal's xsum library, which is written in C. Its directory has
four files:

```{r}
xsum <- file.path(root, pkgs$path[pkgs$name == "Xsum"])
list.files(xsum)
```

`Package.toml` says where the source lives:

```{r}
str(toml_read(file.path(xsum, "Package.toml")))
```

`Versions.toml` has one table per release, keyed by version number and
holding the git tree hash of that release:

```{r}
names(toml_read(file.path(xsum, "Versions.toml")))
```

`Deps.toml` and `Compat.toml` are keyed by version *ranges*: `[0]` covers
every 0.x release, `[1]` every 1.x release, `["1.3-1"]` releases from 1.3 up
to the end of 1.x.

```{r}
str(toml_read(file.path(xsum, "Deps.toml")))
```

This is as far as the registry goes. Xsum 0.x downloaded its binary with
`BinaryProvider`; Xsum 1.x depends on `xsum_jll`, the compiled xsum library.
So the registry shows that Xsum calls compiled code. It cannot say the code
is C: `xsum_jll`'s own files name only its wrapper repository.

```{r}
str(toml_read(file.path(root, pkgs$path[pkgs$name == "xsum_jll"], "Package.toml")))
```

The language is in the Yggdrasil recipe, outside the registry.

## Every package

Reading `Package.toml`, `Versions.toml` and `Deps.toml` for every package
parses some 44,000 small documents.

```{r}
read_all <- function(file) {
  lapply(file.path(root, pkgs$path, file), function(f) {
    if (file.exists(f)) toml_read(f) else list()
  })
}
info <- read_all("Package.toml")
versions <- read_all("Versions.toml")
deps <- read_all("Deps.toml")
```

Almost every package is on GitHub. `subdir` marks a package that lives in a
subdirectory of a larger repository:

```{r}
pkgs$repo <- vapply(info, `[[`, "", "repo")
pkgs$subdir <- vapply(info, function(x) !is.null(x$subdir), NA)
sort(table(sub("^https?://([^/]+)/.*$", "\\1", pkgs$repo)), decreasing = TRUE)
sum(pkgs$subdir)
```

The most released packages, and how many releases were later yanked:

```{r}
pkgs$n_versions <- lengths(versions)
yanked <- function(v) sum(vapply(v, function(e) isTRUE(e$yanked), NA))
pkgs$n_yanked <- vapply(versions, yanked, 0L)
head(pkgs[order(-pkgs$n_versions), c("name", "n_versions", "n_yanked")], 10)
sum(pkgs$n_yanked)
```

### Dependencies of the latest release

To ask what a package depends on *now*, take its latest release and keep
the `Deps.toml` sections whose range contains it. A range is one version or
two joined by `-`; a short bound such as `1` stands for every `1.x.y`.
Pre-releases (`1.0.0-rc1`) are skipped and build numbers (`+0`) ignored.

```{r}
version_parts <- function(v) {
  as.integer(strsplit(sub("[-+].*$", "", v), ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
}

latest <- function(v) {
  v <- names(v)[!grepl("-", names(v))]
  if (!length(v)) return(NA_character_)
  v[order(numeric_version(sub("\\+.*$", "", v)), decreasing = TRUE)][1]
}

# -1, 0 or 1 as version v is below, within or above a (possibly short) bound
compare <- function(v, bound) {
  b <- version_parts(bound)
  d <- which(v[seq_along(b)] != b)
  if (length(d)) sign(v[d[1]] - b[d[1]]) else 0
}

in_range <- function(v, range) {
  bounds <- trimws(strsplit(range, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  lo <- bounds[1]
  hi <- bounds[length(bounds)]
  (lo == "*" || compare(v, lo) >= 0) && (hi == "*" || compare(v, hi) <= 0)
}

deps_at <- function(d, v) {
  if (is.na(v)) return(character())
  v <- version_parts(v)
  hit <- Filter(function(r) in_range(v, r), names(d))
  sort(unique(as.character(unlist(lapply(d[hit], names)))))
}

pkgs$latest <- vapply(versions, latest, "")
pkgs$deps <- Map(deps_at, deps, pkgs$latest)
pkgs$deps[[which(pkgs$name == "Xsum")]]
```

The most depended-on packages at their latest releases. Standard libraries
such as `LinearAlgebra` are not registered, so they are left out:

```{r}
used <- table(unlist(pkgs$deps))
head(sort(used[names(used) %in% pkgs$name], decreasing = TRUE), 15)
```

## Packages with compiled code

The registry records metadata, not source, so it cannot say which language
a package is written in. Dependencies come close:

* a `_jll` package *is* compiled code;
* a package that depends on a `_jll` calls compiled code;
* a package that depends on `CxxWrap`, or on `libcxxwrap_julia_jll`, wraps
  C++;
* a binary that depends on `CompilerSupportLibraries_jll` needs GCC's runtime
  libraries: `libgfortran` (Fortran), `libstdc++` (C++) or `libgomp`
  (OpenMP), without saying which.

```{r}
uses <- function(names) vapply(pkgs$deps, function(d) any(d %in% names), NA)
pkgs$calls_jll <- vapply(pkgs$deps, function(d) any(endsWith(d, "_jll")), NA)
pkgs$cxx <- uses(c("CxxWrap", "libcxxwrap_julia_jll"))
pkgs$gcc_runtime <- uses("CompilerSupportLibraries_jll")

with(pkgs[!pkgs$jll, ], c(
  packages = length(name),
  call_a_jll = sum(calls_jll),
  wrap_cxx = sum(cxx)
))
```

Ordinary packages that wrap C++ through CxxWrap:

```{r}
pkgs$name[!pkgs$jll & pkgs$cxx]
```

The binaries other packages depend on most:

```{r}
jll_used <- unlist(pkgs$deps[!pkgs$jll])
head(sort(table(jll_used[endsWith(jll_used, "_jll")]), decreasing = TRUE), 15)
```

Binaries that need GCC's runtime libraries. This is where Fortran libraries
such as Arpack, HSL or Sundials are found, mixed with C++ and OpenMP ones:

```{r}
gcc <- pkgs[pkgs$jll & pkgs$gcc_runtime, "name"]
length(gcc)
head(sort(gcc), 40)
```

Telling these apart needs the build recipes in Yggdrasil, or the packages'
own source; the registry has taken us as far as it can.
